successCriteria.description: src/shared/error.types.ts exists and exports NotFoundError, ValidationError, and ConflictError classes, each extending the native Error class with correct prototype chain and stack-trace capture
src/shared/base.repository.ts exists and exports a generic IBaseRepository<T> interface declaring findById, findAll, create, update, and delete methods
src/shared/base.repository.ts exports an abstract BaseKnexRepository<T> class whose constructor accepts a Knex instance, providing partial implementations of IBaseRepository<T>

Jest unit tests exist in tests/unit/shared/ covering all three error classes (instantiation, message, instanceof checks) and the BaseKnexRepository contract (abstractness, constructor, method signatures)

constraints: Error classes must extend the native Error class with proper prototype chain (Object.setPrototypeOf or equivalent) so instanceof checks work correctly
BaseKnexRepository<T> must be abstract — it cannot be instantiated directly; concrete module repositories (e.g., KnexLeaveRepository) extend it

IBaseRepository<T> is a generic interface parameterized on the entity type T; findById returns Promise<T | null>, findAll returns Promise<T[]>, create/update/delete return Promise<T> or Promise<void> as appropriate
BaseKnexRepository constructor accepts a Knex instance (imported from the knex package) and stores it as a protected field for subclasses to use
No any type — use unknown with type guards per the no-any constraint in HARNESS.json
Tests must pass with npx jest tests/unit/shared/
outOfScope: Module-specific repositories (e.g., KnexLeaveRepository, ILeaveRepository) — these are Phase 2
Knex migrations, seeds, or knexfile.ts — Phases 6 and 7
Service, controller, route, or model implementations for any module
Integration tests — only unit tests in tests/unit/shared/ are in scope

ambiguities.description: "Partial implementations" in BaseKnexRepository — which methods are implemented vs left abstract? The intent says the class "provides partial implementations" but doesn't specify which CRUD methods get concrete implementations and which remain abstract for subclasses.
options: Implement all five CRUD methods (findById, findAll, create, update, delete) using Knex with a required abstract getTableName() method
Implement only findById and findAll as concrete; leave create, update, delete abstract
Make all methods concrete with sensible Knex defaults, allowing overrides

ambiguities.description: Exact method signatures for IBaseRepository<T> — the intent names five methods (findById, findAll, create, update, delete) but does not specify parameter types (e.g., what type is the id? string? number? what does create accept — a full T or a DTO?)
options: findById(id: string): Promise<T | null>; findAll(): Promise<T[]>; create(entity: Omit<T, 'id'>): Promise<T>; update(id: string, entity: Partial<T>): Promise<T>; delete(id: string): Promise<void>
